description:
Create a new AIDE working file from its blank template, under its canonical name. It never overwrites: a request for a file that already exists, filled or empty, is a no-op reported as a skip line — remove a file first with aide_cleanup to replace it. New files start with their starting value: an intent spec alignment: unreviewed, a plan or todo list status: proposed. Handles the naming rules, so never pick a name yourself: in a module folder, intent specs are .aide by default, but become intent.aide when research.aide exists in the same folder. Creating a research.aide auto-renames any existing .aide to intent.aide. The project root intent spec always lands at .aide/intent.aide: pass directory ".aide" or "." (both mean the project's .aide folder for intent, research and both). A bare .aide/.aide left by an older project, with no intent.aide beside it, is renamed to .aide/intent.aide with its content kept; if .aide/intent.aide exists, nothing changes. Folders are never treated as spec files. A plan needs an intent spec beside it: scaffolding a plan in a folder with no intent spec (.aide or intent.aide; a research.aide alone does not count) is refused and creates nothing — write the folder's intent spec first. For a root-level plan, pass directory ".aide".

Types:
- intent — Strategy, contracts, anti-patterns
- research — Sources, data, patterns (triggers rename of existing .aide)
- both — Creates research.aide + intent.aide pair
- todo — QA re-alignment document for QA agents
- plan — Architect's implementation plan; refused unless the folder already holds an intent spec
- session — The project's session record, always at .aide/session.aide whatever directory you pass: the empty placeholder with every section heading. Its single source; never write the placeholder by hand.

directory.description: Directory where the .aide file(s) will be created. For the project root intent spec pass ".aide" or "."; it lands at .aide/intent.aide

type.description: Type of file to create: intent, research, both, todo, plan, or session (always .aide/session.aide)
